gap: No result ChatGPT got gives a live price for each hour of runtime on a 350 W EverFlo-class concentrator, or names the cheapest maker-store setup that covers a full 8-hour night (3,294 Wh needed at 0.85). On 2026-11-14 that was the EcoFlow DELTA Pro at $1,799 for about 8.7 h. The BLUETTI Elite 300 at $1,199 is the cheapest per hour (about $164/h) but runs out about 40 minutes short of 8 hours, and the BLUETTI Apex 200 + B300K at $2,199 gives about 12.9 h at about $170/h.
standout_why: I compared against blackoutwise.com/will-it-run/home-oxygen-concentrator-5l (cited), willitrunpower.com/best-power-station-for/oxygen-concentrator (cited) and the answer ChatGPT gave. Both pages list hours per station at 350 W and how many Wh 8 hours needs, so the runtime half of this is already covered. BlackoutWise gives only price ranges checked by hand on 2026-10-09 and says they are 'not live prices'. WillRun gives no prices, only 'Check price on Amazon' links. Neither page works out dollars per runtime hour, and neither names the cheapest in-stock maker-store setup that gets past 8 hours. ChatGPT's top pick, the Elite 300, is shown at 7.3 h with no note that it falls short of a full night.
decides: The finding splits the pick by need. For an evening outage up to about 7 hours, the BLUETTI Elite 300 ($1,199, about 7.3 h) is the best value at about $164 per runtime hour. For a full 8-hour night on a 350 W unit, the Elite 300 is not enough. The cheapest single box that covers it is the EcoFlow DELTA Pro ($1,799 at us.ecoflow.com, about 8.7 h). The BLUETTI Apex 200 + B300K bundle ($2,199, about 12.9 h) costs $400 more but gives about 4 more hours and a lower cost per hour ($170 vs $206). The BLUETTI AC200L, our current expandable row, was sold out at BLUETTI US on 2026-11-14, and so was the Anker F3800 Plus at ankersolix.com. A backup oxygen tank from the supplier comes first, whatever station the shopper picks.
